name: cooling
description: Use when the engine runs hot or stays cold, the heater blows cold, the gauge moves oddly or coolant is lost: coolant now plus a cold-start trip.
instructions: Call run_skill {"name":"cooling"}: it reads the coolant temperature now (0105) and, when trips are recorded, the warm-up curve of the latest trip that started cold. It never asks the driver to wait for a warm-up.
When no cold-start trip exists, say the warm-up could not be judged and suggest recording the next cold start with trip recording for a later check.
With coolant sensor or thermostat codes (P0115-P0119, P0128, P2183), open fault_codes and use read_dtcs_detail before blaming the thermostat.
interpret: 105 °C or more now is hot (warn); 115 °C or more is overheating: the engine should be stopped (critical).
A cold start (40 °C or less) driven 15 min or more that never reaches 75 °C points to a thermostat stuck open (often with P0128).

Reaching 80 °C takes more than 20 min (petrol) or 25 min (diesel) after a cold start: a slow warm-up, an early sign of a thermostat opening too soon. Diesels warm slowly at idle, so judge driven trips only.
A recorded trip that peaked at 105 °C or more points to overheating under load: coolant level, fan, water pump or head gasket.
A cold-start trip that ended before the engine reached 80 °C (too short, warmup_not_judged) judges neither the warm-up nor the thermostat: say so, never call the warm-up normal.
A coolant reading that jumps, or disagrees with the gauge, points to the sensor rather than the cooling system.

golf-plus-2009-20tdi: This car has P2183 among its known codes (coolant temperature sensor 2, radiator outlet, G83): G83 is not the 0105 sensor, but a G83 fault can upset fan control; check it before blaming the thermostat.
